items.title: AI company starts paying employees in Bitcoin
points: The firm pays salaries directly in Bitcoin rather than fiat (government-issued currency like dollars or euros).
Employees can hold the Bitcoin or convert it to fiat, keeping flexibility over how they are paid.
Signals growing acceptance of crypto as a legitimate compensation method in the tech sector.

items.title: Banco Santander adds Bitcoin to corporate holdings
points: The Spanish multinational bank bought Bitcoin for its balance sheet, a first-tier institutional endorsement.
Marks a shift from establishment-bank skepticism toward treating Bitcoin as a legitimate asset class.

items.title: Bitchat mesh app keeps Indian protesters online during internet shutdowns
points: Bitchat uses mesh networking (phones relay messages device-to-device without any central server or internet connection) to work during blackouts.
Indian protesters used it to organize and communicate while the government cut connectivity.
Shows real-world censorship-resistance utility of decentralized communication tools.

items.title: ZKPoSP proposed to shield Bitcoin from quantum attacks
points: AmericanFortress proposes replacing Bitcoin's elliptic-curve signatures with zero-knowledge proofs (math that proves you know a secret without revealing it), letting users prove wallet control without exposing keys to quantum computers.
Existing wallet addresses would stay intact under the scheme.
Prototype benchmarks: 12–13 seconds to generate a proof, 9–10 milliseconds to verify.
Adoption needs coordination across wallets, exchanges and miners; no network has implemented it, echoing the contentious BIP-110 debate (a proposed Bitcoin protocol improvement).

items.title: Robinhood posts record $1.31B quarter as prediction markets take over growth
points: Q2 revenue hit a record $1.31 billion, with prediction markets (platforms where users bet on real-world outcomes) replacing spot crypto trading as the growth engine.

Robinhood Chain, an Ethereum layer-2 network built on Arbitrum technology (a add-on network that batches transactions for faster, cheaper settlement than Ethereum's main chain), targets institutional trades and tokenized stocks.
Strategy shifts the platform from retail trading toward institutional infrastructure and on-chain financial products.

items.title: Fake Flare Network staking site drained $8.5M in XRP
points: Seoul police say a fraudulent staking site (staking: locking up crypto to earn rewards) stole $8.5 million in XRP.
Scammers built credibility with fabricated Wikipedia entries and YouTube videos.

items.title: Luno cuts 20% of global staff
points: CEO James Lanigan cited automation and a pivot to institutional services over retail trading.
Reflects wider exchange consolidation favoring institutional clients and automated systems.

sections.title: ZKPoSP: Bitcoin's Quantum-Resistant Solution
points: AmericanFortress proposes replacing Bitcoin's elliptic curve signatures with zero-knowledge proofs, enabling users to prove wallet control without exposing individual keys to quantum attacks.
Prototype benchmarks show 12-13 seconds for proof generation and 9-10 milliseconds for verification—acceptable for most use cases but requiring protocol upgrades.

Adoption requires coordination across wallets, exchanges, and miners with no network having implemented the scheme yet, similar to the contentious debate over BIP-110 (a proposed Bitcoin improvement protocol).

sections.title: Robinhood's Shift to Institutional Markets
points: Q2 revenue hit record $1.31 billion, up significantly as the platform transitions from retail trading toward institutional infrastructure using its new Ethereum layer-2 network.
Prediction markets now drive growth instead of spot crypto trading, with the platform betting heavily on tokenized assets and on-chain financial products for institutional clients.
Robinhood Chain, built on Arbitrum technology, enables faster, cheaper transactions for institutional trades compared to mainnet Ethereum.

sections.title: Luno and Crypto Staffing Trends
points: Luno cut global staff by 20%, with CEO James Lanigan citing automation and a shift toward institutional services rather than retail trading as the reason.
The layoff reflects broader industry consolidation as exchanges prioritize institutional clients and automated systems over manual trading operations.
